strategy.observation: SavvyCal’s mission is to reduce friction and awkwardness in scheduling time with people.
strategy.offer_link: Integrating scheduling links into HubSpot and Salesforce workflows would move scheduling into the systems teams already use, which can reduce back-and-forth and make the booking process feel less awkward—directly aligned with SavvyCal’s stated mission.
hypotheses: The founder may be looking for ways to deepen SavvyCal’s role inside revenue-team workflows.
SavvyCal may see CRM-native scheduling as a useful distribution or retention lever.
Their customers may benefit from placing booking links inside HubSpot and Salesforce automations rather than only on standalone booking pages.
strategy.angle: SavvyCal already exists to remove scheduling friction; putting scheduling links inside HubSpot and Salesforce workflows is one way to remove it where teams actually work.
strategy.fit_reason: SavvyCal is a scheduling company with a mission explicitly centered on reducing scheduling friction, so an integration that embeds booking links into HubSpot and Salesforce workflows is a plausible and relevant extension of that value proposition.

draft.subject: Scheduling in CRM
draft.body:
SavvyCal’s mission is already about reducing friction in scheduling.

My guess is putting booking links inside HubSpot and Salesforce workflows would cut some of the back-and-forth teams deal with, since they can schedule where the work already happens.

I build integrations that place scheduling links inside CRM workflows. If this feels like a useful direction, would you be the right person to ask whether it belongs in the product roadmap?
